UX/UI design

Case studies, the studio I design for, and how I work.

Plug Our Potholes

UX/UI case study: a community app, developed with Floodlight Studios, where people report potholes, vote for the next area and donate to fix their own roads.

The problem: badly maintained roads and constant damage to our cars. We'd all had enough, but complaining doesn't fill a pothole.

What I made: a space where communities come together to donate cash and fix their own roads. Developed with Floodlight Studios.

How it works

01 REPORTShare your location or search a road to report a pothole.
02 VOTEVote for the next area you want fixed.
03 DONATEPut some hard-earned rand towards fixing the roads.
04 TRACKSee how much has been raised and how many potholes are left.
05 COUNTDOWNWatch the countdown to filling day and share it with others.

Style guide

Loud yellow, near-black and chunky Sora type make every screen bold and consistent, with clear button and error states. Isometric illustrations add the flare, so reporting something terrible feels almost fun.

The screens

Report it, vote for it, fund it, then watch it get filled. Local slang like "Potholes are just kak" talks the way drivers do, and the Everyday Heroes list thanks neighbours by name, building a community.

Fleet Receiving

UX/UI case study: Fleet, a stand-alone receiving system for a distribution centre that tracks every touch point of an offload, so bottlenecks show up.

The challenge

Quantities, quality & bottlenecks

A distribution centre runs on how many items it can offload per hour. One slow delivery delays the rest of the day.

The unseen problem

Where do bottlenecks start?

The receiving team couldn't see where delays began, or how one badly run delivery affects the day.

What I made

Fleet, a receiving system

A stand-alone system tracking each touch point of receiving, so bottlenecks show up across the whole offload cycle.

User flow

Progressive disclosure and a clear, ordered structure kept the primary user flow simple, easy to navigate and easy to discover.

Iterations

With a concise layout and structure in place, we explored every option for colour, copy and styling, keeping to the brand's look and feel while staying accessible to users.

The app

EASE OF USEA simple, clear interface.
SCANNINGFast data capture, with every point of offload and quality control tracked.
USER ROLESEach role in the delivery gets its own view for tracking and reporting.
YARD ENTRY & EXITSecurity scans the licence disk and logs arrival and departure times.
RECEIVINGMetrics captured throughout the offload, from quality control to truck departure.

Web admin panel

App data syncs into a live dashboard: average offload time, deliveries processed, bay efficiency and delivery tracking, for daily and monthly comparison. Admins manage permissions, user lists and reports from the same place.

A Journey With Kal

An illustrated, animated Instagram diary about living with Kallmann syndrome and acromegaly: informative, a bit funny, and shared by people around the world.

An animated Instagram diary about my life with Kallmann syndrome and acromegaly. Simple, informative and a bit funny, so people respect what we deal with instead of feeling sorry, and others living with it know they're not alone.

The animations

Each animation simulates a symptom, from a lost sense of smell to vertigo, educating viewers while being fun to watch and learn from.

The responses

The diary reached people around the world, who shared it and their own stories. Even famous motion designers like Ben Marriott commented on it.

iMvelo Care

Corporate identity for iMvelo, a mobile spa and wellness centre for women that specialises in care for the elderly.

A corporate identity for iMvelo Care, built around a logo they supplied. iMvelo is a mobile spa and wellness centre for women in KwaZulu-Natal, and it specialises in care for the elderly.

The identity

It rests on the brand’s values: natural, calm and safe spaces for women, and organic treatments. Plant shapes, soft pastels, and a purple and green for natural care.

Out in the world

The identity carries onto the van, the website, the promotion stands and the products iMvelo sells.

Takkie Wash & Squeaky Kleen

Team lead on a rebrand of two cleaning brands for a new in-store partnership, so customers can tell which brand does what.

I led a team on a brand strategy for two cleaning businesses that had just joined forces. Customers couldn’t tell which brand did what, so we made each one its own brand and made the partnership known.

Two brands

Colour and copy keep them apart: Takkie Wash is here for the kicks, Squeaky Kleen is the laundromat. Short, punchy lines make each cleaning service obvious.

In motion

Each brand got its own animated loop with its line and address, ending on the news that it has partnered with the other.

Pulse Hybrid Inverter

Packaging for a backup power inverter that has to sell itself in store. Bronze at the 2020 SA Gold Pack Design Awards and a Top 100 international entry.

Packaging for a backup power inverter that has to sell itself in store, with no sales rep and no manual, and show it’s part of a bigger solar kit. Bronze at the 2020 SA Gold Pack awards and a Top 100 international entry.

The idea

I created Pulse, a brand about protecting people’s productivity, with the inverter at its heart. It’s for small businesses and homeowners.

The features

A simple line system guides you around the box. A QR code opens a live wattage calculator, and there’s a number to call, WhatsApp or SMS. Yes, I used the box.

Saddler Repositioning

Repositioning Saddler from a white-label business to an on-trend fashion accessory brand: “Your World. Your Way.”

Saddler is a family-owned brand with a 30-year history, positioned as Smart Heritage. The brief: reposition it as a modern fashion accessory brand. The new line: Your World. Your Way.

The new position

A go-to lifestyle and fashion accessory brand, for the urbanite and the fashion enthusiast. Quality accessories made to represent you, wherever you’re going.

The look

The brown is the brand’s past and a new blue is its fashion future. The horseshoe stays, because it’s already the sign on Saddler’s buildings.

The campaign

Instagram stories and posts carry the line, from giveaways to new collections.

Retro Grade

A T-shirt range I designed to celebrate 50-plus years of gaming and esports, and the two-page publication that presents it.

A two-page magazine spread for a product I designed: T-shirts that celebrate 50-plus years of gaming and esports, based on the games that defined their genres.

I looked at Memphis design, modern cyberpunk illustration and pixel art, for a retro style with a modern spin. The research was extremely enjoyable.

Jonsson Workwear: Siyapusha

Group lead on the campaign strategy to launch Jonsson’s lifestyle footwear, The Kalahari’s, which drove the launch collateral and a packaging redesign.

I led the group that planned the relaunch of Jonsson Workwear’s Kalahari’s, a veldskoen. The Khoisan made the shoe to go greater distances, and farmers made it the shoe we know today. So the relaunch sells one value the shoe and the brand share: reliability.

Go anywhere

The pack sells a reliable journey: hard work, quality and moving forward. The name, Siyapusha, says the same. Built for the pressure.

Your own box

Order online and the box can carry an illustration of a picture you choose, so it becomes a collector’s piece.

About

Vick Does Creative

I can't pick one label. Artist, designer, animator, fighter, builder, developer: I've been all of them before lunch. What I actually do is take the resources, context and knowledge in front of me and rework them into something that solves the problem. So I just say it plainly: I am creative.

Since age 12

My dad owns a full-scale branding company. Other kids had chores. I had print jobs to set up. I learned production before I learned to drive, and I've been working creatively ever since.

Indian, South African

I'm Indian, born and raised in South Africa. At 198 cm I'm hard to miss, so look for the tall one in the corner with a sketchbook.

Forever student

I never finish learning, and I like it that way. Right now that means a theology degree alongside full-time design work. Faith shapes why I create, not only what I create.

Off the clock

  • Family: I come from a close family: both my parents and three brothers. My dad runs a full-scale branding company, which is where my design life started at 12.
  • Lindy: My partner, and a big part of my world. She has heard every idea on this site at least twice.
  • Faith: I'm a non-denominational Protestant Christian, finishing a theology degree at Doxa Deo & SATS (2023–2026). Faith shapes why I create, not only what I create.
  • Jiu-Jitsu: I train and compete. On the mat, as in design, technique and patience beat brute force.
  • Hiking & nature: Long walks uphill, for fun. It's research with better views.
  • Dungeons & Dragons: Worlds, characters and stories built together around a table. It's also where I learned to plan for players who ignore the plan.
  • Dogs: I love dogs. No further research needed.
  • Drawing: I'm always sketching. Everything on this site started in pencil.
